fields.h1: Build a Credit Application Form for New Trade Accounts
fields.hero_description: Build a credit application form that checks trade references by email and sends large requests to the credit manager.
fields.features_heading: What a Business Credit File Holds
fields.features_subheading: A Word template comes back scanned, with phone numbers to chase. These six features turn it into a file you can decide on.
fields.feature_1:
The questions a credit manager asks

Asks for the legal name and EIN, then years in business, the amount requested and trade and bank references. Required fields stop a file from arriving with the bank reference blank.
fields.feature_2:
An email to every trade reference

Emails each reference two questions: the highest credit it extends and how fast the applicant pays. Replies land on the applicant's row, and silence for three days gets a reminder.
fields.feature_3:
Uploads read into fields

Reads uploaded resale certificates and financial statements into fields like certificate number and annual revenue. A field read with low confidence goes to a person to confirm.
fields.feature_4:
Terms of sale signed on screen

Captures the owner's signature on your terms of sale and on any promise to pay personally. The file stores the signer's name, the time they signed, and the terms version they saw.
fields.feature_5:
Routing set by the amount requested

Sends small requests to an analyst and large ones to the credit manager. A Slack alert flags each new file, and every approved amount is logged with who approved it and when.
fields.feature_6:
Source code in your GitHub repo

Exports the full app to your GitHub on paid plans. A developer can connect it to your ERP or accounting system through its API, or you can describe any change in a prompt instead.

fields.usecase_heading: Credit Applications by Type of Supplier
fields.tab_content_1:
References answer by email before the first order

Harbor Foods Supply opens restaurant accounts on net 30 terms. Each owner lists three suppliers the restaurant buys from, and each one gets an email asking what limit it allows and whether the restaurant pays on time. Juniper Bistro has two of three replies in, and the third gets a reminder after three days.
fields.tab_content_2:
Requests over $25,000 go to the credit manager

Cobalt Packaging's credit policy has one line: any request over $25,000 needs two years of financial statements and the credit manager's review. Smaller requests go to an analyst. When Pinecrest Foods asks for $40,000, the form will not submit without both statements, and the file reaches the credit manager in Slack.
fields.tab_content_3:
Resale certificates read into the account record

Contractors opening an account at Granite Ridge Building Supply attach a resale certificate. The form reads the certificate number and expiration date onto the account. On the Bellmont Builders file, the date came back with low confidence, and a clerk checks it against the scan before the account opens.
fields.tab_content_4:
The owner signs before any equipment leaves

Summit Equipment Rental will not send a skid steer out on account until the paperwork is done. New customers apply on a phone at the counter, and the last screen shows the full promise to pay personally, and the owner signs it with a finger. Dario Vance signed at 7:40 AM, and his file went to credit review complete.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Credit Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set a credit policy, build a credit application form around it, and send every applicant a decision.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep protected traits off the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Set your standard terms, such as net 30, and the limit at which a request moves to a senior reviewer. Decide what each tier requires: trade references below that line, financial statements above it. Each question on the form should trace back to the policy.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act bars discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, or age, or because income comes from public assistance. Regulation B also limits marital status questions on individual unsecured credit.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for trade references from suppliers who sell to the applicant on terms, plus a bank reference. Get an email address for each contact, not only a phone number. A supplier the applicant pays in advance has no payment record to report.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give Emergent the policy as written, plus the uploads you need from applicants, such as financial statements or a resale certificate. It builds the application and a database table for the accounts. Changing a question later takes one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put the terms on the last screen
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put your terms of sale on the final screen, with the owner's promise to pay personally if your policy calls for one and a line allowing you to contact the listed references. The signer types or draws a signature, and the app keeps a copy of the exact terms shown to them.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Read the references, then set a limit
fields.howto_step_6_des: Check what each trade reference reported: the highest credit it extended and how late the applicant pays, if ever. Compare that with the amount requested. The credit manager records the approved limit and the reason for it on the account, where anyone reviewing it later can read it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Regulation B gives a creditor 30 days after a completed application to approve, counteroffer or deny it. For trade credit, the rule is notice within a reasonable time, orally or in writing. A denied applicant can ask for the reasons in writing within 60 days.

faq_plan.q: What is a credit application form?
faq_plan.a: A credit application form is what a customer fills out to ask a supplier or lender for credit, such as an account on net 30 terms. A business applicant gives its tax ID, the credit it wants, and the suppliers and bank that can vouch for it. The applicant signs to confirm the answers and to let you contact those references.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a credit application form?
faq_plan.a: Write your credit policy first, then describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the fields and uploads, and who reviews which amounts. Emergent builds the form and the database table behind it. Run one real application through it before you share the link, and change any question later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide an example of a credit application form?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide an example of a credit application form?

prov.original: Can you provide an example of a credit application form?

faq_plan.a: Yes. Picture a food distributor opening restaurant accounts, with five sections on its form. The first covers the company and its EIN, the second the amount and terms requested. Then come three trade references with email addresses, one bank reference, and a signature on the terms of sale. Each section maps to one decision the credit team makes.

faq_plan.q: Can applicants upload documents to a credit application form from a phone?
faq_plan.hint: How to make embeddable credit application forms fcra compliant?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An upload field on a phone takes a photo of a resale certificate or a PDF of last year's financial statements. Ask for uploads by tier: a certificate from every reseller, statements only above your review limit. The app Emergent builds can read each upload into named fields on the account. The same step works on a driver application form, for a photo of the license.

faq_plan.q: Which questions can a simple credit application form leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out any question your credit policy never uses. A simple credit application form for small trade accounts can stop at the legal name, EIN, billing contact, amount requested, two trade references, and a signature on your terms. Save the bank reference and financial statements for requests above your review limit. A small account then has fewer fields to fill in.

faq_plan.q: How many trade references should a credit application form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for three. One reference that never replies then still leaves two answers to judge. State the minimum on the form itself. The sample notice in Regulation B includes insufficient number of credit references provided as one of the reasons a creditor can check.

faq_plan.q: What does a credit application form for a business ask that a consumer one does not?
faq_plan.a: It asks about the company instead of the person: the legal name, EIN, years in business, trade references, and a bank reference. Regulation B's appendix has four model credit application forms, each designated for use in a particular type of consumer credit transaction. To screen tenants instead of trade customers, start from a rental application form.

faq_plan.q: Can I change a credit application form after customers start using it?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Describe the change in a prompt, such as a second bank reference or a new upload, and Emergent changes the form and its database. Accounts already on file keep their rows in a database you own. Test the new version with one application before you publish it, and tell anyone with an open file if a required field was added.

faq_plan.q: How do I connect a credit application form to my accounting system?
faq_plan.a: Connect it through the accounting system's API. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API, syncing data in and out. An approved account can then arrive in your ledger with its limit and terms. Pick one system as the record for each limit, and let the other read it.

faq_plan.q: What should a credit application form collect about the business owner?
faq_plan.a: Collect the owner's name and home address, their share of ownership, and a signature if the owner backs the account personally. Ask only for what your credit policy uses, and limit who can open that section of the file. If you need a full profile of a person for something other than credit, a personal information form fits better.
